item.title: Expanded Access to Generative AI Tools at FAS
item.description:
Hi All,

I just want to bring your attention to an e-mail from May 6 about “Expanded Access to Generative AI Tools at FAS” that everyone should have received. Essentially there are three tiers of access to AI tools: 1) Free, 2) API key, and 3) License. I just want to clarify how IQSS is approaching access to each of these tiers. The form mentioned in the June 6 e-mail is only in regard to “License access”.

item.title: Brendan Case
item.description:
Brendan Case

Associate Director for Research, Human Flourishing Program

Email: brendan_case@fas.harvard.edu

Dr. Case’s research bridges the humanities and social sciences to explore the nature, distribution, and determinants of a flourishing life, with a particular focus on dispositions such as love, and on key institutional pathways to flourishing, such as religious communities and marriage.

item.title: Cameron Harvey
item.description:
Cameron Harvey

IT Client Support Services Associate

Email: help@iq.harvard.edu

Cameron Harvey joined IQSS in 2018 as an IT Client Services Support Specialist. He provides members of the IQSS community with IT desktop support. Previosly Cameron worked in the role of IT Systems Administrator for an EMS service provider, as well as IT Systems Support for a medical firm.

item.title: Cheng Shi
item.description:
Cheng Shi

Front-End Developer, Dataverse

Email: cshi1@g.harvard.edu

Cheng Shi graduated from the University of Southern California in 2023 with a master’s degree in Data Science, following her bachelor’s degree from Penn State University. She currently serves as a front-end developer for Dataverse at IQSS. In this role, she develops high-performing single-page applications, ensuring optimal user experiences through efficiency and precision. Her interests extend to broader web application development, where she continues to explore innovative solutions to enhance functionality and user engagement.

item.title: Dan Yuan
item.description:
Dan Yuan

Data Science Project Management Specialist

Email: tyuan1@fas.harvard.edu

Dan Yuan serves as a Data Science Project Management Specialist at IQSS, coordinating and managing data science projects and providing technical support to researchers across the institute.

item.title: Danny Ebanks
item.description:
Danny Ebanks

Research Associate

Email: debanks@g.harvard.edu

Danny recently earned his PhD at Caltech in Quantitative Social Sciences, where he developed his research interests in Political Methodology, American Politics and Congress. His research focuses on latent variable models, Bayesian statistics, legislatures, and natural language processing. At IQSS, he strives to develop and implement statistical methods, to understand the latest in machine learning and AI, and innovate in these areas in ways small and large to better understand our political world. He is always eager to chat about research and statistics, so feel free to reach out. Outside of research, he is a lifelong runner who hails from New York.

item.title: Don Sizemore, II
item.description:
Don Sizemore, II

Developer, Dataverse; Systems Programmer, UNC

Email: don.sizemore@gmail.com

Don Sizemore became involved with IQSS through the Dataverse project when he joined the Odum Institute in 2015. He is the primary author of the Dataverse-Ansible role, a consultant through the Global Dataverse Community Consortium, and attempts to support the Dataverse community over its various communication channels. He holds a Master of Information Science from UNC’s School of Information and Library Science, but highly cherishes his undergraduate minor in music performance on pipe organ.

item.title: Dwayne Liburd
item.description:
Dwayne Liburd

Library Assistant, Data Science

Email: dliburd@hmdc.harvard.edu

Dwayne Liburd is the Data Technology Support Associate in Data Acquisition and Archiving. His responsibilities include assisting the Manager of Data Acquisition, providing assistance on using Dataverse services, and providing user support for Dataverse. Dwayne also maintains the Henry A. Murray Research Archive Dataverse. He performs the cataloging of the metadata, storage of data related to the archive, and data processing, preservation, and dissemination of the original holdings of the Archive.

item.title: Ellen Kraffmiller
item.description:
Ellen Kraffmiller

Principal Software Architect and Data Engineer

Email: ekraffmiller@hmdc.harvard.edu

Ellen Kraffmiller is a software engineer who has been at IQSS for over ten years. Previously, she worked in software consulting, financial services and biotech industries. She has contributed to the Dataverse and Consilience projects. She has expertise in distributed computing, machine learning and natural language processing.

item.title: Emily Lawrence
item.description:
Emily Lawrence

Linux Systems Administrator, HMDC

Email: elawrence@hmdc.harvard.edu

Emily majored in Electronic Media, Arts and Communications at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, and worked at BU for six years before joining IQSS in 2016.

item.title: Emma Loayza
item.description:
Emma Loayza

Office Manager

Email: egloayza@iq.harvard.edu

Emma joined IQSS in May of 2024. Prior to that, she worked as an Office Manager in both the Library Student Employment Program and the Digital Ventures Lab at Boston University Libraries. Her current work at IQSS focuses on physical space management, as well as assisting with a variety of projects for the IQSS Operations team. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Archaeology from Boston University, and enjoys reading, writing, and cooking in her free time.

item.title: Evan Sarmiento
item.description:
Evan Sarmiento

Front End Systems Software Developer

Evan Sarmiento is a Front End Systems Software Developer at IQSS, specializing in user interface development and front-end technologies for the institute’s various research and data management platforms.

item.title: Farhan Ghrairi
item.description:
Farhan Ghrairi

Assistant Director of Finance

Farhan Ghrairi serves as the Assistant Director of Finance at IQSS, overseeing financial operations and providing strategic financial leadership for the institute.

item.title: Gabrielle Stone
item.description:
Gabrielle Stone

Events Coordinator

Email: gstone@iq.harvard.edu

Gabrielle is a professional event planner who has worked with Harvard University for 10 years. She graduated from the University of Connecticut with a Bachelor’s degree in English and has a Certificate of Special Studies in Administration and Management from Harvard Extension School, focusing on nonprofit management, marketing and public relations, museum administration, and fundraising. Her previous career was in publishing.

item.title: Gustavo Durand
item.description:
Gustavo Durand

Dataverse Technical Lead / Architect

Email: gdurand@iq.harvard.edu

Gustavo Durand is the Technical Lead and Architect of Dataverse, an open source data repository platform developed by IQSS at Harvard University. Gustavo has been on Dataverse in many roles since its inception and in his current role, leads the architecture and technical design of the platform, reviews code from internal and and external developers, assists the Dataverse Community contributors, and overall works closely with the Development Project Manager. He began his Java programming career at Cambridge Technology Partners in 1997 and has over 20 total years experience as a software developer and consultant.

item.title: James D Myers
item.description:
James D Myers

Developer, Dataverse Core Development Team

Email: jim.myers@computer.org

Dr. Myers is an independent software architect, designer, and developer currently working in the Dataverse community through the Global Dataverse Community Consortium (GDCC) and the Qualitative Data Repository (QDR). He received his B.A. in Physics from Cornell University (1985) and his Ph.D. in Chemistry from the University of California at Berkeley (1993). He has more than three decades of experience in the development and deployment of Cyberinfrastructure for research, education, and industrial application and has participated in the planning and execution of multiple large community cyberinfrastructure projects for the US NSF, ONR, and DOE. Dr. Myers has been active in the development of provenance and content management standards and has led efforts to design and develop data-intensive hardware and software systems. As a co-PI on SEAD DataNet project, Dr. Myers helped develop a scalable mechanism for the long-term preservation of scientific research results based on semantic web and cloud technologies and leveraging active and social curation approaches to increase data re-use and lower lifecycle costs. He has development experience using multiple languages (Java, Scala, PHP, Javascript, C/C++) and technologies (including relational and document databases, semantic web, preservation formats, dev/Ops, Docker, AWS).

item.title: Jeffrey Blossom
item.description:
Jeffrey Blossom

GIS Service Manager, Center for Geographic Analysis

Jeffrey Blossom is the GIS Service Manager at the Center for Geographic Analysis (CGA). He provides expert guidance and support to researchers utilizing geographic information systems and spatial analysis methodologies in their work.

item.title: Jinjie Liu
item.description:
Jinjie Liu

Data Science Specialist

Email: jinjie_liu@fas.harvard.edu

Jinjie works as a Data Science Specialist on the Data Science Services team at IQSS. She holds a master’s degree in Economics from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and a PhD in Political Science from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She further finishes her master’s study in Computer Science from Cleveland State University. Jinjie is interested in formal modeling, statistical modeling, machine learning, data manipulation and management as well as political economy and comparative research methods. She has experience in statistical programs including Stata and SPSS. She also has experience with general-purpose programing languages including Python, C/C++, SQL, Java, Matlab.

item.title: Jorge Dasilva
item.description:
Jorge Dasilva

Senior Sponsored Research Administrator

Email: jdasilva@iq.harvard.edu

Jorge joined the Sponsored Finance team at IQSS in July 2023 as a Sr. Sponsored Research Administrator. He supports several principal investigators affiliated with IQSS. He is described as “a seasoned finance professional with over 25 years of experience in both education and the business sector.” Jorge joined Harvard in 2003 as a Grants Manager at the New England Primate Research Center and subsequently held roles with the Department of Psychology and the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. In these positions he “managed complex financial reporting and analysis, lead business operations initiatives and assisted faculty and staff with portfolio management.” He lives with his wife and 3 children (15-year-old boy/girl twins and 14-year-old son) and in his spare time enjoys spending time on his boat and attending his children’s sporting activities.

item.title: Joshua Cetron
item.description:
Joshua Cetron

Data Science Specialist

Email: jcetron@iq.harvard.edu

Josh is a data scientist, social scientist, and methodologist with a background in psychology, neuroscience, and multivariate statistics. As a Data Science Specialist at IQSS, he provides methods and analysis consulting services and collaborative support to Harvard-affiliate researchers across the sciences, focusing on experimental methods, exploratory analysis, and regression modeling of empirical data in R and python. He joined IQSS in June 2023 after completing his Ph.D. in Psychology at Harvard, where he studied psychological and neural representations of social and political information, including political propositional knowledge and social group attitudes. During graduate school, he developed an interest in methods and analysis development and support as a Teaching Fellow for multiple graduate-level statistics courses, teaching advanced statistical methods and collaborating with statisticians to develop new analytical methods. Prior to his Ph.D., he completed his B.A. in neuroscience at Dartmouth College, where he studied neural representations of concept knowledge acquired through classroom-based learning. Outside of work, he enjoys playing music, rock climbing, and exploring coffee shops in Somerville and Cambridge.

item.title: Juan Pablo Tosca
item.description:
Juan Pablo Tosca

Senior Software Developer, Dataverse

Email: juan_tosca@iq.harvard.edu

Juan Pablo Tosca is a Senior Software Developer who joined IQSS in 2023 to work on the Dataverse project. He previously worked at the Harvard Graduate School of Education as a Senior Software Developer focused on Java and Spring applications. He became involved with Dataverse and the Containerization Working Group before officially joining the team, and has contributed to Dataverse releases since version 6.1. He is originally from Xochimilco (meaning “place of the flowers” in Nahuatl) in Mexico City, and came to the United States in 2014 after completing his MBA at Universidad del Valle de Mexico. He is fluent in English and Spanish. In his free time, he enjoys discussing immigration, music, and technology.

item.title: Julian Gautier
item.description:
Julian Gautier

Product Research Specialist

Email: juliangautier@g.harvard.edu

Julian Gautier joined IQSS in September 2016 as a product research specialist for the Data Science and Product Research team, responsible for providing and extending Dataverse metadata support, and helping collect software requirements from product leaders and its community of users. Shortly before joining the team, Julian finished a Masters program in Library and Information Science at UCLA, studying and practicing user experience research and information architecture. His interests outside of work include volunteering in UX communities and playing basketball and tennis.

item.title: Junyi Chen
item.description:
Junyi Chen

GIS Analyst, Center for Geographic Analysis

Email: junyichen@fas.harvard.edu

Junyi Chen is a master’s student in Machine Learning and Data Science at Northwestern University, beginning her studies in fall 2024. She graduated Cum Laude from Stony Brook University in December 2021, earning dual bachelor’s degrees in mathematics & applied mathematics and statistics, which she completed in 2.5 years. She also minored in computer science and participated in the WISE (Women in STEM) honors program. After graduation, Junyi worked as a full-time data analyst at Transwarp Technology in China for two years, focusing on the supply chain and finance fields. She is also certified as a Data Management Professional Associate and has developed a strong interest in big data and spatial data analysis. Driven by a passion for using data to drive industry growth and research advancements, she has contributed remotely to multiple CGA projects and is looking forward to expanding her work in geospatial analysis with the IQSS.

item.title: Keri Lemasters
item.description:
Keri Lemasters

Senior Sponsored Research Administrator

Email: klemasters@iq.harvard.edu

Keri joined the sponsored finance team at IQSS in February of 2019 and has worked in sponsored administration for nine years. She supports several principal investigators affiliated with IQSS in pre-award and post-award services for federal and private foundation awards. Prior to IQSS, she worked for five years as a Financial Analyst with the Office for Sponsored Programs at Harvard. At OSP, she was a key contributor in managing the Financial Reporting Application Portal (FRAP), which “drastically increased monthly automation of financial reports and invoices to over 60%.” In 2016, she assisted HUIT/FSS with the FIRST project, which successfully transitioned FRAP automation into GMAS in April 2018, enabling new applications for sponsored compliance and financial reporting (Transaction monitoring and Financial Dashboard). She also contributed to university-wide financial award set up and revisions of thousands of funded projects feeding into Harvard’s peripheral financial systems. She “was nominated as a Harvard Hero for remarkable sacrifice for co-workers, departments, and the University in 2015.” She holds a Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Humanities from Michigan State University.

item.title: Leonid Andreev
item.description:
Leonid Andreev

Senior Developer, Dataverse Project

Leonid Andreev is a Senior Developer on the Dataverse Project at IQSS. He brings extensive expertise in software development and has been instrumental in advancing the Dataverse platform, an open-source data repository software used by research institutions worldwide.

item.title: Linda Christlieb
item.description:
Linda Christlieb

Finance Associate

Email: lchristlieb@iq.harvard.edu

Linda has been with Harvard University since 2012. Prior to joining IQSS in 2015 in the Finance and Administration Division, Linda worked as a Faculty Assistant and Executive Assistant for an economics professor for three years. Her current responsibilities include payroll, processing payments and reimbursements and many other finance transactions for IQSS and it’s affiliates. Linda holds a Bachelor’s degree from Southern Connecticut State University and has two sons in college.

item.title: Lisa Galvin
item.description:
Lisa Galvin

Academic Affairs Coordinator

Email: lgalvin@iq.harvard.edu

Lisa joined IQSS in November 2011. Prior to this, Lisa worked as a temporary Human Resources Coordinator in Harvard’s Faculty of Arts and Sciences (FAS) HR department. Lisa earned her Professional in Human Resources (PHR) certification in June 2013 and also holds a Bachelor’s degree. She enjoys reading, television, movies, music, and keeping up with current events. Lisa lives with her husband in Cambridge.

item.title: Liz Salazar
item.description:
Liz Salazar

Communications Coordinator

Email: lsalazar@iq.harvard.edu

Liz Salazar has been at IQSS since 2010, working her way into her current role via management of the IQSS website and social media. As Communications Coordinator, she oversees the Institute’s online presence, publicity, and external communications, plus updates to the IQSS affiliate database. She previously worked at the Harvard Foundation (part of Harvard College Student Life), and before Harvard she was at Boston University’s Center for English Language.

item.title: Maria Martins
item.description:
Maria Martins

Executive Assistant

Email: mmartins@iq.harvard.edu

Maria joined IQSS in March 2016. She previously served as an Executive Assistant in Harvard’s Office for Sponsored Programs (OSP) for eight years. Before Harvard, she worked at The Inn at Harvard as Office Manager and at the Hilton Back Bay and Hilton Logan Airport as a Sales and Catering Assistant. She holds a “Bachelors of Science in Business Administration from Newbury College.” In her free time, she “enjoys spending time with her family, running, and volunteering.”

item.title: Michael O'Brien
item.description:
Michael O’Brien

Academic Affairs Coordinator

Email: mobrien@iq.harvard.edu

Michael joined IQSS in May 2024 as an Academic Affairs & HR Coordinator, having previously served as interim Office Manager in the IQSS’ Business Operations Division. He provides academic personnel and staff support for all IQSS faculty affiliates across the University, focusing on academic policy advisement, classification and compensation, recruitment, Visa administration, leaves administration, and general HR policies. His prior experience includes public health consultancy at John Snow Inc., healthcare administration at Boston Children’s Hospital, and operations at BXP. He “graduated summa cum laude from the University of Massachusetts Boston” with a BA in Sociology.

item.title: Mike Reekie
item.description:
Mike Reekie

Senior Project Manager for Engineering

Email: mreekie@iq.harvard.edu

Mike Reekie is the Senior Project Manager for Engineering and Technical Operations at IQSS, Harvard. He handles day-to-day project management for the IT Operations team and Engineering software development projects for the DevOps team.

His background includes serving as Director of Systems Engineering at Momentum Telecom, where his team modernized and scaled nationwide infrastructure supporting data-over-cable and wholesale VoIP networks, managing provisioning for 900K cable modems for 300 independent cable ISPs.

item.title: Noah Greifer
item.description:
Noah Greifer

Data Science Specialist

Email: ngreifer@iq.harvard.edu

Noah Greifer has been a member of the Data Science Services team at IQSS since August 2021. He earned his BS in Psychology from UC San Diego, worked in the Office of Institutional Research at Reed College, and earned his MA and PhD in Quantitative Psychology at UNC Chapel Hill before a brief post-doc in the Department of Mental Health at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. He specializes in causal inference methods for observational studies, including propensity score matching and weighting methods, and has written or maintains several R packages designed to implement these methods, including ‘WeightIt’, ‘MatchIt’, ‘cobalt’, and ‘MatchThem’, among others. He loves mint chip ice cream, new music, and sudoku.

item.title: Philip Durbin
item.description:
Philip Durbin

Software Developer, Dataverse Project

Email: philip_durbin@harvard.edu

Phil Durbin holds a Psychology degree from the University of Dayton and works as a Software Developer on the Dataverse Project at IQSS. He was part of the team that rewrote Dataverse to be more inclusive of all science. He is enthusiastic about the growth of Dataverse installations to over a hundred, and actively participates in the community through the mailing list, chat room, and monthly community calls. He sends out the monthly Dataverse Community News and looks forward to the annual Dataverse Community Meeting. He is passionate about open source (having given a talk at JavaOne about running an open source project) and created a dataset called “Open Source at Harvard” in Harvard Dataverse. He co-founded the codecraft mailing list, has a project called Crossroads, and makes mobile games with his kids. He blogs at blogs.harvard.edu/pdurbin and his personal website is greptilian.com.

item.title: Rand Kiessig
item.description:
Rand Kiessig

Manager, IQSS Computer Lab Services

Email: rkiessig@iq.harvard.edu

Rand Kiessig joined IQSS in May 2012 and has led IQSS Computer Lab Services since 2015. A California native, Rand has lived across the U.S. — from Washington State to North Carolina to Massachusetts — with stints in Mexico and Spain along the way. Before coming to Harvard, he held a range of technical roles at organizations including Microsoft, Verio, Data General, and Iron Mountain.

item.title: Robert Treacy
item.description:
Robert Treacy

Principal Software Architect, Dataverse

Email: rtreacy@hmdc.harvard.edu

Bob Treacy is a Principal Software Architect and Data Engineer. He came to IQSS in 2006 at the beginning stages of the Dataverse Project and participated in the initial architecture, design and development of the system. He worked on a project for survey research, the Consilience project for text analysis, differential privacy, and maintained the Zelig project and various other R packages when they were hosted on CRAN. He has been working with Java since 1995, when he was at Fusion Systems Group, a consulting firm which worked closely with Sun Microsystems. He has over 35 years in software development for manufacturing, financial systems, education course management, news delivery and various web companies. In addition to Java, he has developed in Scala, C/C++, Python, and R. He has worked with various relational databases and NoSQL databases. His first distributed systems project in the early 90s involved integrating stove-piped legacy terminal-based manufacturing systems using modern UIs and in recent years has worked with Hadoop and Spark for machine learning and AI. He is currently involved with fine-tuning local Large Language Models using FAS RC on Dataverse data. He has worked with the AWS and Azure cloud platforms.

item.title: Roy Guyton
item.description:
Roy Guyton

IT Client Support Services Associate

Email: rguyton@hmdc.harvard.edu

Roy is a graduate of Willamette University where he received a BA in Spanish Literature and International Studies in Salem, OR. He also received his Ed.M for Technology in Education from the Harvard Graduate School of Education. Additionally, Roy has taken graduate courses at NIH, MIT and the Division of Continuing Education (DCE) at Harvard University. Roy was employed with the Harvard Graduate School of Education for 12 years where he ran the student help desk, and employed 10 years at DCE as a graduate teaching assistant. He spent three years in Costa Rica as a US Peace Corps volunteer working with IBM, MIT, Omar Dengo Foundation and the Costa Rican Department of Education on a national computer education program. He holds extensive contracting experience since 1992 in the area of technology in education. Roy was also a board member of several non profit organizations.

item.title: Sarah Duncan
item.description:
Sarah Duncan

IT Operations Manager, IQSS/Harvard-MIT Data Center

Email: slduncan@fas.harvard.edu

Sarah Duncan is the IT Operations Manager at IQSS/Harvard-MIT Data Center. She supports Social Science research using Linux and holds an undergraduate degree in Engineering and Applied Science and a Masters in Divinity, both from Harvard. Previously, she served as webweaver for Harvard’s Department of Genetics at the Medical School, spent eleven and a half years handling IT for the Harrison/Wiley x-ray crystallography labs in Biochemistry, and most recently worked eight years at WGBH as a UNIX, Storage, and Windows Systems Administrator. She lives in Boston’s North End with her wife Reay and two cats, speaks Spanish and Tamil (learned during a college year abroad in Madurai, India), and enjoys reading, learning new things, travel, cooking, yoga, crafts, and glass bead making and fusing.

item.title: Soner Taskaya
item.description:
Soner Taskaya

Associate Director of IT Client Services

Email: staskaya@iq.harvard.edu

Soner Taskaya is Associate Director, IT Client Services at IQSS. He joined HMDC/IQSS as an IT Support Specialist in August 2003. Previously, he served as a Junior Systems Administrator at a startup software company for four years and worked in IT support at Harvard Medical School as a Client Support Representative for two years. He earned his B.A. in Business Management and Marketing from Curry College. In his free time, he enjoys traveling, hiking with his dog, snowboarding in winter, and golfing and fishing in summer.

item.title: Sonia Barbosa
item.description:
Sonia Barbosa

Associate Director of Dataverse Support, Data Curation, and Murray Archive

Email: sbarbosa@hmdc.harvard.edu

Sonia Barbosa is the Associate Director of Dataverse Support, Data Curation, and the Murray Archive. Her responsibilities include developing and promoting the use and benefits of the Dataverse Software and outreach and acquisitions of data for the Harvard Dataverse Repository. Sonia leads training on data curation and consults with users on organizing, cleaning, and preparing data for sharing and preservation, and provides curation support and guidance for users of the tool. Sonia also manages the data housed at the Murray Archive, a human subjects social science data archive housing longitudinal data on the lives of women. She is responsible for curation of the collection, preservation of data related to the archive, and data processing and dissemination. Sonia works closely with the Dataverse development team to increase awareness of the needs of the research community and provides usability feedback on the Dataverse features. She has over 27 years of data curation and management experience in the social sciences. She holds a BA in Psychology with a concentration in African American Studies from the College of the Holy Cross, 1995, and a BSN from Simmons College, 2009.

item.title: Stephen Kraffmiller
item.description:
Stephen Kraffmiller

Software Developer, Dataverse Project

Email: skraffmiller@hmdc.harvard.edu

Stephen has been a developer on the Dataverse Project since 2010. He is involved in all aspects of the Dataverse project, from the front end UI development to the back end business logic. For the Dataverse project he was the lead developer for custom dataset metadata fields, persistent identifiers, guestbook and download tracking. He also implemented dataset templates and external query tools. He has given three presentations at JavaOne conferences over the years including “jQuery Integration with JSF 2 Libraries” with Mike Heppler and “Custom Bean Validation” with Gustavo Durand. Currently he is spearheading the effort to make Dataverse data available via the Google Data Commons. In his spare time he enjoys running, reading, cooking and following the career of a talented playwright who happens to be his daughter.

item.title: Steven Winship
item.description:
Steven Winship

Software Developer and Systems Administrator

Email: steven_winship@iq.harvard.edu

Steven is working on the Dataverse Project.

item.title: William Horka
item.description:
William Horka

Systems Administrator, Harvard-MIT Data Center

Email: whorka@hmdc.harvard.edu

William Horka serves as a Systems Administrator at the Harvard-MIT Data Center, providing technical support and managing computing infrastructure for social science research.

item.title: Ying Chen
item.description:
Ying Chen

Research Associate & Data Scientist, Human Flourishing Program

Ying Chen is a Research Associate and Data Scientist with the Human Flourishing Program at IQSS. She applies her expertise in data science and quantitative methods to research exploring human well-being and flourishing.

item.title: 2023 OpenDP Community Meeting Recap
item.description:
The 2023 OpenDP Community Meeting was held on September 29th at Harvard University, bringing together researchers, practitioners, and developers focused on differential privacy. The event was organized in conjunction with the TPDP (Theory and Practice of Differential Privacy) workshop, marking the first in-person gathering for the OpenDP community since the project’s inception.

Attendees explored the latest developments in the OpenDP Library, discussed real-world deployment challenges, and shared insights on building privacy-preserving data analysis systems. Presentations covered topics ranging from new algorithmic implementations to user experience improvements in the DP Creator application.

item.title: 2024 OpenDP Community Meeting - Recap and Survey
item.description:
The 2024 OpenDP Community Meeting was held August 22-23 at Harvard University, once again joining forces with TPDP (Theory and Practice of Differential Privacy). The two-day event brought together differential privacy researchers, software developers, and data practitioners from academia, government, and industry.

Key highlights included demonstrations of new OpenDP Library features, panel discussions on differential privacy deployment challenges, and breakout sessions on topics such as privacy budget management and user-facing tools. Participants also engaged in collaborative problem-solving around real-world privacy scenarios.

item.title: A focus on flourishing: Newest IQSS program
item.description:
The Human Flourishing Program, IQSS’s newest scientific program, combines social science and philosophy to understand the factors that lead to a good life. Directed by Tyler VanderWeele, the program integrates knowledge from empirical research and the humanities on topics including religion, virtue, work, purpose, forgiveness, marriage, and family.

The program’s interdisciplinary approach sets it apart from traditional academic research centers. By bringing together researchers from psychology, epidemiology, philosophy, and theology, the Human Flourishing Program examines well-being through multiple lenses simultaneously, producing insights that no single discipline could achieve alone.

item.title: A Love of Learning and Helping Others Succeed: Wendy Guan Retires
item.description:
By Colleen Walsh

A map covered in red dots hangs on Wendy Guan’s office wall. The dense rosy points obscure what lies beneath until a closer look reveals Italy, Sicily, and the tip of Tunisia.

Those vibrant points enabled Harvard’s Francis Goelet Professor of Medieval History Michael McCormick to connect the dots. He had turned to Guan and her team at Harvard’s IQSS Center for Geographic Analysis (CGA) to help track the path of the Plague of Justinian (541–ca. 750 CE) for his medieval history class.

item.title: A New Industry-Academic Initiative at IQSS
item.description:
IQSS has announced a new initiative designed to transform academic social science research into market-ready startup ventures. The new industry-academic connections being built will help social scientists increase scholarship impact, harvest data and resources from the commercial world for research, and enable universities and businesses to learn from each other more effectively.

As part of this effort, IQSS welcomes the “Startup Foundry” (with a new name to be chosen soon), which has been moved from its previous home at Harvard Business School. The initiative is led by its director and newest IQSS team member, Debi Kleiman, and is supported by contributors Kelly and Carla Kimball.

item.title: Adaner Usmani
item.description:
Adaner Usmani

Assistant Professor of Sociology

He is an Assistant Professor of Sociology and Social Studies at Harvard University, having earned his Ph.D. in Sociology from New York University in May 2017. From 2017 to 2019, he served as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the Watson Institute at Brown University.

His research centers on questions of inequality — why some people flourish while others suffer, and what explains why “movements or policies emerge to challenge or moderate this inequality” in certain places.

item.title: Affiliate Spotlight: Adam Stefkovics
item.description:
Adam Stefkovics is a visiting researcher at IQSS with a Fulbright scholarship, an assistant lecturer at Eotvos Lorand University in Budapest, and director of polling at the Szazadveg Foundation. His research focuses on survey methodology, political polling, and public opinion analysis in Central European democracies.

During his time at IQSS, Stefkovics has been working on projects related to survey design and measurement, benefiting from the institute’s expertise in quantitative methods and access to collaborative research resources. His work bridges Hungarian and American academic traditions in political science and survey research.

item.title: Affiliate Spotlight: Jacob Brown
item.description:
Jacob is a resident graduate student at IQSS who is graduating this spring with a PhD in Government and Social Policy. If you see him around CGIS, be sure to wish him congratulations and good luck!

What is the focus of your work?

“Political geography and political behavior in American politics.”

What’s something you like about IQSS?

“The grad students have semi-regular dinners that are a lot of fun.”

item.title: Affiliate Spotlight: Maria Ballesteros
item.description:
Maria Ballesteros is a graduate student and resident affiliate at IQSS, pursuing her PhD in the Department of Government at Harvard. Her research focuses on political behavior, institutions, and methodology, with particular attention to how political systems shape citizen engagement and representation.

As a GSAS Prize Fellow, Ballesteros brings exceptional academic credentials to her work at IQSS, where she benefits from the institute’s collaborative environment, research computing resources, and community of quantitative social scientists. She regularly participates in IQSS seminars and workshops.

item.title: Affiliate Spotlight: Sascha Riaz
item.description:
Sascha Riaz is a Harvard Government PhD student (G5) and resident affiliate at IQSS. His research examines political economy, with a focus on how historical institutions shape contemporary political and economic outcomes, particularly in South Asian contexts.

As a resident affiliate, Riaz has been an active member of the IQSS community, participating in seminars, collaborating with other researchers, and leveraging the institute’s data science resources for his dissertation work. His methodological approach combines quantitative analysis with historical case studies.

item.title: AI leaps from math dunce to whiz
item.description:
IQSS affiliate Michael Brenner, the Michael F. Cronin Professor of Applied Mathematics and Applied Physics, explains how recent AI advancements have opened new possibilities for mathematical application. What was once considered a fundamental limitation of artificial intelligence—its inability to perform complex mathematical reasoning—has been dramatically overcome by newer model architectures.

Brenner discusses how these advances enable researchers to tackle problems that were previously computationally intractable, from solving differential equations to discovering new mathematical theorems. The implications extend across scientific disciplines where mathematical modeling plays a central role.

item.title: Al Roth
item.description:
Al Roth

George Gund Professor of Economics, Emeritus

Alvin Elliot Roth is the Craig and Susan McCaw professor of economics at Stanford University and the Gund professor of economics and business administration emeritus at Harvard University.

Roth has made significant contributions to the fields of game theory, market design and experimental economics, and is known for his emphasis on applying economic theory to solutions for “real-world” problems.

item.title: Al Roth Receives Nobel Prize in Economics
item.description:
IQSS affiliate Al Roth (Harvard Business School) and Lloyd S. Shapley were awarded the 2012 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel for their work on the theory of stable allocations and the practice of market design. The prize recognized how their research had moved from abstract theory to practical applications that improve people’s lives.

Roth’s work on market design has led to better systems for matching kidney donors with patients, assigning students to schools, and placing medical residents in hospitals. His approach combines game theory with careful empirical observation to design mechanisms that produce stable, efficient outcomes in markets where prices alone cannot do the job.

item.title: Alejandro Kantor
item.description:
Alejandro Kantor

IQSS Fellow

Alejandro is an IQSS Fellow working on research related to course data from HarvardX and the EdX platform with Professor Dustin Tingley and the Office of the Vice Provost for the Advancement in Learning. Through his research, Alejandro develops statistical models as well as interactive visualizations. He is also a Senior Project Analyst at the Office for Faculty Affairs of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences.

item.title: Alessandro Vespignani
item.description:
Alessandro Vespignani

Professor, Northeastern University

Alessandro Vespignani is Sternberg Distinguished Professor at Northeastern University with appointments in the College of Computer and Information Sciences, the Bouve’ College of Health Sciences and the Department of Physics.

He received his undergraduate degree and Ph.D., both in physics, from the University of Rome “La Sapienza,” in 1990 and 1993 respectively. He completed postdoctoral research at Yale University and Leiden University. He worked at the International Center for Theoretical Physics (UNESCO) in Trieste and at the University of Paris-Sud in France as a member of the National Council for Scientific Research (CNRS) before moving to Indiana University in 2004. Before joining Northeastern, he was “J.H.Rudy Professor of Informatics and Computing at Indiana University” and served as Director of the Center for Complex Networks and Systems Research and Associate Director of the Pervasive Technology Institute.

item.title: Alice Sommer
item.description:
Alice Sommer

LMU Munich

Alice is a PhD candidate in Human Biology at the Ludwig-Maximilian University (LMU) of Munich. At Harvard, she is an Institute Fellow working in Marie-Abèle Bind’s Lab at the Department of Statistics of FAS. She completed an MSc in Statistics at the KU Leuven in Belgium. Her research interests focus on applying causal inference methods to understand environmental epidemiology problems. Her projects include the estimation of effects of air pollution on multiple sclerosis relapses and on the human gut microbiome.

item.title: Alina Herderich
item.description:
Alina Herderich

Visiting Fellow, Digital Emotions Lab

Alina Herderich is a predoctoral researcher at the Digital Emotions Lab led by Amit Goldenberg at HBS. Her home university is the Graz University of Technology. The majority of her undergraduate and graduate studies comprised psychology, which she complemented with a substantial amount of computer science. Since then she enjoys being a Computational Social Scientist who uses data science tools, especially from natural language processing, to shed new light on old and newly arising psychological questions. Her fields of interest are manifold, but she mainly focuses on emotion regulation theory and measurement (e.g., building a data-driven taxonomy of emotion regulation strategies) and collective moderation of public online spaces (e.g., citizen counter speech on social media platforms). Visit her website to find out more.

item.title: Alisha Holland
item.description:
Alisha Holland

Associate Professor, Department of Government

Alisha Holland studies the comparative political economy of development with a focus on urban politics, social policy, and Latin America. Before joining the Harvard faculty, she was an Assistant Professor in the Politics Department at Princeton University and a Junior Fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows. Her first book, Forbearance as Redistribution: The Politics of Informal Welfare in Latin America (Cambridge Studies in Comparative Politics), examines the politics of enforcement against property law violations by the poor, such as squatting, street vending, and electricity theft. Her articles have appeared in the American Journal of Political Science, American Political Science Review, Comparative Political Studies, and World Politics, among others. She is currently writing a book on the politics of mass infrastructure projects in Latin America.

item.title: Alyssa A. Goodman
item.description:
Alyssa A. Goodman

Robert Wheeler Wilson Professor of Applied Astronomy

Alyssa Goodman holds the Robert Wheeler Willson Professorship of Applied Astronomy at Harvard University, serves as Co-Director for Science at the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study, and is a Research Associate of the Smithsonian Institution. Her “research and teaching interests span astronomy, data visualization, and online systems for research and education.”

In her astronomical work, Goodman and her research group at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics “study the dense gas between the stars.” They focus on how interstellar gas forms new stars, using observational techniques ranging from X-ray to radio wavelengths. She was Principal Investigator of The COMPLETE Survey of Star-Forming Regions, which mapped three large star-forming regions in our Galaxy. More recently, she and collaborators have focused on using dense filamentary clouds they call “The Bones of the Milky Way” to map galactic structure at high resolution.

item.title: Amy Yeboah Quarkume
item.description:
Amy Yeboah Quarkume

Associate of IQSS; Assoc Professor, Howard University

Dr. Amy Yeboah Quarkume, known as “Dr. A,” is described as “a daughter of Africa, scholar, filmmaker, data scientist” and Associate Professor of Africana Studies at Howard University. She holds a PhD in African American Studies, two Master of Arts degrees in Sociology and African American Studies, and is pursuing an MS in Data Analytics and Computational Social Science from UMass, along with data science credentials from Harvard Extension School and MIT.

item.title: An Amazing 2025 Dataverse Community Meeting
item.description:
The IQSS Dataverse Core team recently returned from the 2025 Dataverse Community Meeting, which was hosted by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The event represented the culmination of two and a half years of intensive development work, resulting in several major milestones for the Dataverse Project.

Key Highlights

  • A new React-based frontend, expected to be available in production in July 2025
  • The launch of Dataverse Hub and Dataverse Marketplace
  • Significant advancements in AI readiness, including full support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Croissant-ML metadata schema. Dataverse was selected as one of the data repositories for the NeurIPS25 conference, described as “the most important AI conference of the year”
  • AutoSage — an AI Metadata helper built on open source large language models, fully trained at IQSS on the complete Harvard Dataverse data, along with the forthcoming Dataverse Knowledge Graph
  • A powerful External Search Tool that uses natural language queries to interrogate the Dataverse repository alongside traditional keyword and facet-based search
  • New integration with high performance computing infrastructures, including the internal FAS-RC cluster, via a tool called LOOP that connects OpenOnDemand and Dataverse seamlessly (a collaboration between the Dataverse and HPC teams at IQSS)
  • New Large Data Support services deployed at scale

Community Growth

The Dataverse community continues to expand, with worldwide installations growing from 70 in 2022 to over 135 today. The meeting showcased contributions from institutions and developers across the globe.

item.title: Ana Trisovic
item.description:
Ana Trisovic

Research Scientist

Ana Trisovic is a Research Scientist at MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL), working at the FutureTech Lab studying AI’s societal and scientific impacts. She holds a PhD in Applied Computer Science from the University of Cambridge & CERN (2018) and is affiliated with CSAIL, MIT Sloan School of Management, and Harvard’s Institute for Quantitative Social Science.

Her research interests include AI, Science & Society—examining foundation model adoption, AI-driven automation, and the risks of de-democratization. Her work translates large-scale empirical findings into policy recommendations.

item.title: Andrea Blasco
item.description:
Andrea Blasco

Research Associate, LISH

Andrea Blasco is a research associate at IQSS at Harvard University, working for the Laboratory for Innovation Science at Harvard (LISH). His research interests span Industrial Organization, Economics of innovation, and Media Economics. Much of his work focuses on understanding the relationship between R&D and the legal system of IP rights. An equally important part of his research analyzes key economic concepts and issues affecting new and traditional media. Andrea holds a PhD in Economics from the University of Bologna, and a Master M2 from Toulouse School of Economics.

item.title: Andrei Shleifer
item.description:
Andrei Shleifer

John L. Loeb Professor of Economics

John L. Loeb Professor of Economics at Harvard University, Andrei Shleifer holds an undergraduate degree from Harvard and a Ph.D. from MIT. Before coming to Harvard in 1991, he has taught at Princeton and the Chicago Business School. Shleifer has worked in the areas of comparative corporate governance, law and finance, behavioral finance, as well as institutional economics. He has published six books, including The Grabbing Hand (with Robert Vishny), and Inefficient Markets: An Introduction to Behavioral Finance, as well as over a hundred articles. Shleifer is an Editor of the Quarterly Journal of Economics, and a fellow of the Econometric Society, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and the American Finance Association. In 1999, Shleifer won the John Bates Clark medal of the American Economic Association. According to RePEc, Shleifer is the most cited economist in the world.

item.title: Andrew Ballard
item.description:
Andrew Ballard

Assistant Professor, Department of Government, American University

Andrew Ballard is an Assistant Professor of Government at American University specializing in Congressional institutions and elections, applied statistics, and machine learning.

item.title: Andrew Ho
item.description:
Andrew Ho

Charles William Eliot Professor of Education

Andrew Ho is Charles William Eliot Professor of Education at the Harvard Graduate School of Education. He is a psychometrician whose research focuses on test-based educational accountability metrics, addressing “measures of proficiency, growth, value added, achievement gains, achievement gap closure, college readiness, and course completion.” He serves on the National Assessment Governing Board and chairs the Research Committee for the Harvard University Vice Provost for Advances in Learning.

item.title: Angela Lee
item.description:
Angela Lee

IQSS Affiliate; Research Scientist, Facebook

Angela Lee completed a PhD in sociology at Harvard University in 2021. She is currently a Research Scientist at Facebook.

Her dissertation research examined wealth inequality by gender in the United States. She looked at trends in the gender wealth gap over the past three decades, changes in the gender wealth gap over the life course, and wealth inequality between husbands and wives. She has also studied crime and criminal justice, including the causal effect of employment on crime for juvenile offenders and the high rates of dropout in residential drug treatment.

item.title: Angie Acquatella
item.description:
Angie Acquatella

Visitor

Angie is an Assistant Professor at the Toulouse School of Economics who received her PhD in Economics from Harvard University in 2021. Her research focuses on the optimal design of health care policy, specifically public health insurance systems and pharmaceutical payment policy. She pursues policy designs that advance health equity, minimize risk for disadvantaged individuals, and incentivize socially valuable investments. Her work combines methods from optimal tax theory with traditional cost-effectiveness analysis in health economics, situated at the intersection of health economics and public finance.

item.title: Ania Jaroszewicz
item.description:
Ania Jaroszewicz

Postdoctoral Fellow

Ania Jaroszewicz is a behavioral scientist whose work “examines questions related to poverty and inequality,” with current research on how people decide to ask for help.

She “completed her PhD in behavioral decision research at Carnegie Mellon University.” Before that, she worked in consumer protection for the federal government and studied economics and psychology at UC Berkeley. She is “a 2016 recipient of the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship.”

item.title: Anna Taylor
item.description:
Anna Taylor

Team Lead, IT Client Support Services

Anna has been with IQSS/HMDC since 2007.

item.title: Announcing OpenDP Library 0.5
item.description:
The OpenDP Project is excited to announce the release of OpenDP Library 0.5, introducing significant architectural improvements that provide a more flexible and powerful approach to tracking privacy budgets and composing differentially private algorithms. This release represents a major step forward in making differential privacy more accessible and practical for real-world data analysis workflows.

Version 0.5 introduces enhanced mechanisms for privacy accounting, allowing developers to build more sophisticated differentially private systems with greater precision and control. The flexible privacy tracking framework makes it easier to compose complex analyses while maintaining rigorous mathematical guarantees about privacy loss. These improvements enable data practitioners to extract more utility from their protected datasets while still ensuring strong privacy protections for individuals represented in the data.

item.title: Announcing OpenDP Library 0.8
item.description:
The OpenDP team announced the release of OpenDP Library 0.8, a modular collection of algorithms for building privacy-preserving applications. This version focuses on expanding the library’s capabilities while maintaining its commitment to mathematical rigor and verified privacy guarantees.

Version 0.8 introduces new transformations and measurements, improved documentation, and enhanced interoperability with common data science workflows. The release reflects ongoing collaboration between Harvard’s OpenDP team and the broader differential privacy research community.

item.title: Announcing OpenDP Library 0.9
item.description:
The OpenDP Project is proud to announce the release of OpenDP Library 0.9, a major milestone that expands the modular collection of differentially private algorithms available for building robust privacy-preserving applications. This release brings powerful new capabilities to developers and data scientists who need to extract insights from sensitive data while providing mathematically rigorous privacy guarantees.

Version 0.9 significantly expands the library’s algorithmic toolkit, adding new measurements, transformations, and composition mechanisms that enable more sophisticated privacy-preserving analyses. The modular architecture allows users to construct custom differentially private pipelines by combining building blocks in flexible ways, each with formal privacy proofs that ensure the overall system maintains its privacy guarantees. Enhanced support for common data analysis tasks makes it easier to adopt differential privacy without requiring deep expertise in the underlying mathematics.

item.title: Announcing the 2021 IQSS Graduate Research Grant Recipients
item.description:
The Institute for Quantitative Social Science is pleased to announce the recipients of the 2021 IQSS Graduate Research Grants, a competitive program that provides crucial financial support for dissertation research by graduate students across Harvard’s social science departments. These grants enable students to conduct ambitious research projects that require funding for data collection, fieldwork, specialized software, research assistance, or other resources essential to completing high-quality dissertation work.

The IQSS Graduate Research Grant program reflects the institute’s commitment to supporting the next generation of quantitative social scientists by removing financial barriers to innovative research. Recipients represent diverse disciplines and methodological approaches, from experimental and survey research to computational text analysis and spatial studies. The grants provide students with flexibility to pursue their research visions while benefiting from IQSS’s broader ecosystem of methodological expertise, consulting services, and collaborative community.

item.title: Announcing the 2023 OpenDP Community Meeting
item.description:
The OpenDP Project is thrilled to announce the first in-person OpenDP Community Meeting, bringing together researchers, developers, and practitioners working at the intersection of data privacy, statistical analysis, and open-source software development. This historic gathering marks an important milestone for the OpenDP ecosystem, providing a venue for face-to-face collaboration, knowledge sharing, and community building around practical differential privacy tools.

The meeting will feature presentations on the latest developments in the OpenDP Library, case studies from organizations deploying differential privacy in production systems, and technical workshops that help participants gain hands-on experience with privacy-preserving data analysis. Sessions will cover topics ranging from fundamental concepts for newcomers to advanced techniques for experienced practitioners, ensuring valuable content for attendees at all levels. The gathering also provides crucial opportunities for informal discussions, networking, and collaborative problem-solving that are difficult to replicate in virtual settings.

item.title: Announcing the Magaro Peer Pre-Review Program
item.description: IQSS is proud to announce the launch of the Alexander and Diviya Magaro Peer Pre-Review Program, an innovative initiative designed to improve scholarly research quality and accelerate publication success by providing authors with rigorous peer feedback before journal submission. This program addresses a common challenge in academic publishing: manuscripts often receive first peer feedback many months after journal submission, leading to lengthy revision cycles that slow the advancement of knowledge.

item.title: Anthony Salvanto
item.description:
Anthony Salvanto

Executive Director of Elections, CBS News

Anthony Salvanto is CBS News’ executive director of elections and surveys, where he oversees all polling across the nation and states, heads the CBS News Decision Desk that estimates outcomes on election nights, and appears across CBS News broadcasts and platforms. He is the author of Where Did You Get This Number: A Pollster’s Guide to Making Sense of the World (Simon and Schuster). Anthony’s PhD in political science is from the University of California, Irvine, and his BA from Tufts. His areas of expertise and interest include American politics and elections, public opinion, and survey research methods, and his scholarly writing has appeared in research journals, edited volumes and conference papers covering topics including voting behavior and sampling techniques.

item.title: Antoinette Schoar
item.description:
Antoinette Schoar

Professor, MIT Sloan School of Management

Antoinette Schoar is the Michael M. Koerner Associate Professor of Entrepreneurial Finance at the MIT Sloan School of Management. She has been teaching at Sloan for six years in the areas of corporate finance and entrepreneurship. While starting at Sloan she has developed a new course on Entrepreneurial finance which is a second year elective. Professor Schoar holds a PhD in Economics from the University of Chicago and an undergraduate degree from the University of Cologne, Germany. She received several prestigious scholarships from the German National Scholarship foundation, ministry of commerce and the George Stigler Center at the University of Chicago. She is a member of the American Finance Association and the National Bureau of Economic Research.

item.title: Ariel Procaccia
item.description:
Ariel Procaccia

Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science

Ariel Procaccia is Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science at Harvard University. He “works on a broad and dynamic set of problems related to AI, algorithms, economics, and society.” His honors include the Social Choice and Welfare Prize (2020), a Guggenheim Fellowship (2018), the IJCAI Computers and Thought Award (2015), and a Sloan Research Fellowship (2015). To make his research more publicly accessible, he founded the not-for-profit websites Spliddit.org and RoboVote.org, and he regularly contributes opinion pieces.

item.title: Arthur Kleinman
item.description:
Arthur Kleinman

Esther and Sidney Rabb Professor of Anthropology

Arthur Kleinman is a psychiatrist and anthropologist who has spent over four decades teaching at Harvard Medical School’s Department of Global Health and Social Medicine and in the FAS Department of Anthropology. He chaired the former department from 1989-2000 and the latter from 2004-2007, and held the Presley Professorship at HMS from 1993-2000. From 2008 to 2016, he served as the Victor and William Fung Faculty Director of Harvard’s Asia Center.

item.title: Babak Fotouhi
item.description:
Babak Fotouhi

Post-doctoral Fellow, Program for Evolutionary Dynamics

Babak employs concepts from sociology, behavioral economics, and network science to study human behavior and interaction theoretically and experimentally. Broadly, he studies the linkages and mutual influences of two categories of entities. The first one subsumes social structure, social context, and culture. The second one encompasses perceptions, preferences, behaviors, and interactions. A central strand of his research revolves around human cooperation. It attends to questions such as how altruism, prosociality, and trust, can be promoted to outweigh egoism, what factors strengthen or impair trust, and what is the interplay between social networks and individual cooperative attitudes. Babak received his PhD from the department of electrical and computer engineering at McGill university, after receiving an MSc in physics from Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics. He worked on the mathematics and statistical physics of networks—e.g., evolution of the structure of complex networks (social, biological, and technological), and diffusion of information, influence, and pathogens on social networks. After his PhD, he received an MA in Sociology from McGill. His main focus was quantitative methods and computational social sciences (linking machine learning and data science to sociology). His other interests in sociology are social theory and social psychology. On the methodological side, his main interest is causal inference, particularly for networked data.

item.title: Bailey Moore
item.description:
Bailey Moore

IT Client Support Services Associate

Bailey Moore joined IQSS in 2024 as an IT Client Services Support Specialist. She studied Computer Networking at Lamar Institute of Technology. Originally from Texas, she moved to New York and then Boston. She previously served as a Network Administrator for a School District and worked IT Help Desk for Neches FCU.

item.title: Become an Affiliate
item.description:
About Affiliation

IQSS welcomes scholars who participate in Institute life to become affiliates. Participation opportunities include:

  • Attending seminars
  • Giving talks to the IQSS community
  • Working with IQSS graduate student affiliates
  • Co-authoring or collaborating with IQSS affiliates
  • Serving on committees
  • Reviewing scholarly grant applications
  • Attending events
  • Sharing coffee in the IQSS “Quantina” common space

Affiliation enables graduate students and Harvard Faculty to apply for funding or access IQSS-based services such as Sponsored Research Services.

item.title: Ben Fifield
item.description:
Ben Fifield

Research Scientist, Meta

IQSS Visitor/Affiliate.

item.title: Benjamin Lewis
item.description:
Benjamin Lewis

Affiliate, Dataverse; Director, Open Inference Initiative

Ben Lewis works on open infrastructure for machine-actionable spatial data and auditable spatial inference systems. His current work focuses on improving support for spatio-temporal data and machine-readable metadata in research repositories such as Harvard Dataverse, to make spatial data easier to find, reuse, and incorporate into reproducible workflows.

Ben spent much of his professional career at Harvard’s Center for Geographic Analysis, initially as a spatial data scientist and later as a technology manager. His teams designed and developed a range of widely used open spatial platforms, datasets, and research infrastructure.

item.title: Benjamin Mako Hill
item.description:
Benjamin Mako Hill

Faculty Associate, Berkman Center; Asst Prof, UW

Benjamin Mako Hill is a social scientist, technologist, and activist. In all three roles, he works to understand why some attempts at peer production—like Wikipedia and Linux—“build large volunteer communities while the vast majority never attract even a second contributor.” He is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Communication at the University of Washington and a founding member of the Community Data Science Collective. He is also an Adjunct Assistant Professor in UW’s Department of Human-Centered Designed and Engineering as well as a Faculty Associate at the Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society and an affiliate at the Institute for Quantitative Social Science—both at Harvard University. He has also been a leader, developer, and contributor to the free and open source software community for more than a decade as part of the Debian and Ubuntu projects. He is the author of several best-selling technical books, a member of the Free Software Foundation board of directors and an advisor to the Wikimedia Foundation. Hill has a Masters degree from the MIT Media Lab and a PhD from MIT in an interdepartmental program between the Sloan School of Management and the Media Lab.

item.title: Benjamin Schneer
item.description:
Benjamin Schneer

Assistant Professor of Public Policy, HKS

Benjamin Schneer is an Assistant Professor of Public Policy at Harvard Kennedy School. He studies American Politics, with work focused on three areas: (1) understanding how individuals and groups engage in political expression to influence lawmakers and each other; (2) tracing the effects of electoral institutions on political behavior of citizens and legislators; and (3) “Documenting the long-run career incentives faced by government officials and how these incentives shape policy-making.” He received his PhD in the Department of Government at Harvard University.

item.title: Bernd Resch
item.description:
Bernd Resch

Visiting Scholar, CGA; Professor, IT:U Austria

Bernd Resch is a Full Professor of Geo-social AI at IT:U and a Visiting Scholar at Harvard University’s Center for Geographic Analysis. He completed his PhD in “Live Geography” (real-time monitoring of environmental geo-processes) in collaboration with University of Salzburg and MIT. Before joining IT:U, he served as Associate Professor and Faculty Speaker at University of Salzburg, Research Director at Heidelberg University, and Research Affiliate at MIT. His research focuses on understanding cities as complex systems by analyzing diverse digital data sources, with emphasis on developing machine learning algorithms for human-generated data including social media posts, mobile phone data, and physiological measurements from wearable sensors. These findings apply to urban research, disaster management, epidemiology, and other fields. He received the Theodor Körner Award for his work on “Urban Emotions” and established the iDEAS:lab, a multi-functional outreach and science communication laboratory. He serves as an Editorial Board Member of IJHG, IJGI and PLOS ONE, a scientific committee member of various international conferences (having chaired several), and an Executive Board member of Spatial Services GmbH.

item.title: Better Research VI: Data Sharing with Harvard Dataverse
item.description:
Better Research VI: Data Sharing with Harvard Dataverse

Date: May 20, 2026

Time: 12:30 PM – 2:00 PM EDT

Location: Lamont Library B30 Collaborative Learning Space

A free 1.5-hour in-person workshop on using Harvard Dataverse for data sharing and preservation. Covers how the repository supports research projects, funder/journal compliance, and FAIR data principles. Format includes lecture, demonstrations, and discussion. Participants learn about repository features relevant to their discipline, data type, or funder requirements. Open to Harvard faculty, research staff, postdocs, and students (Harvard ID required). No prerequisites.

item.title: Beyond 100 Installations: Dataverse's Growth and Global Role in Research Data Sharing
item.description:
The Dataverse Project, developed at IQSS, has surpassed 100 installations worldwide, marking a significant milestone in its mission to make research data sharing accessible to scholars globally. This growth reflects the platform’s adoption across universities, research institutions, and government agencies on every continent.

From its origins as the Harvard Dataverse Network, the project has evolved into a truly global infrastructure for research data management. Each installation represents an independent repository where researchers can deposit, share, and preserve their data according to FAIR principles—making it Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable.
