item.title: Bob Treacy: From the Factory Floor to Harvard and 30 Years of Java
item.description: Bob Treacy, Principal Software Architect on the Dataverse Project at IQSS, recently shared his remarkable journey from working on factory floors to becoming a key architect of one of the world’s leading open-source research data repository platforms. His story offers unique insights into the evolution of software development over three decades and the enduring relevance of Java, the programming language that has been central to his career and to the Dataverse platform.

item.title: Bonnie OBrien
item.description:
Bonnie OBrien

Director of Human Resources

Email: bobrien@iq.harvard.edu

Bonnie O’Brien joined IQSS in 2012 and is currently the Director of Human Resources. She provides overall HR leadership and support in the areas of recruitment and retention, employee relations, organizational and policy development, performance management, and oversees academic personnel. Before Harvard, she worked at UC San Diego in a similar HR role. She holds a bachelors degree in liberal arts, a Human Resources Management certificate from UCSD, a Senior Professional in Human Resources (SPHR) certification, and has 20 years of comprehensive HR experience, over 15 of those in higher education. She is currently enrolled in a Master’s program for Industrial-Organizational Psychology.

item.title: Brad Rosen
item.description:
Brad Rosen

Entrepreneur-In-Residence, IQSS Startup Foundry

Brad Rosen is a serial entrepreneur and technology executive with deep experience building and scaling data-driven companies at the intersection of AI, software, and applied research. He is a co-founder and former COO of NODAR, a 3D vision company advancing perception systems for autonomous vehicles, and has led or founded multiple venture-backed companies across enterprise and consumer markets, with successful exits to strategic acquirers including Cisco, Motorola, and others. Brad holds a BS in Electrical Engineering from the University of Colorado and an MBA from MIT Sloan. At the Institute for Quantitative Social Science (IQSS) Startup Foundry, he focuses on helping translate cutting-edge research in data science, causal inference, and AI into commercially viable products and impactful real-world applications.

item.title: Brian Guay
item.description:
Brian Guay

Postdoctoral Researcher, MIT

Brian Guay is a postdoctoral researcher at MIT in the Department of Political Science & Sloan School of Management. His research sits “at the intersection of political behavior and methodology,” focusing specifically on “misinformation and polarization.” His work draws on cognitive and social psychology theories and employs methods including “field experiments, surveys, and natural language processing with social media data.” He earned his PhD from Duke University’s Department of Political Science in spring 2021, where he participated in “the Duke Polarization Lab and Duke Initiative on Survey Methodology.”

item.title: Brian Schaffner
item.description:
Brian Schaffner

Professor of Political Science, Tufts University

Brian Schaffner is the Newhouse Professor of Civic Studies in Political Science and Tisch College at Tufts University. His research focuses on “public opinion, campaigns and elections, political parties, and race and prejudice in American politics.” He co-authored Hometown Inequality: Race, Class, and Representation in American Local Politics and Campaign Finance and Political Polarization: When Purists Prevail.

He serves as a Principal Investigator for the Cooperative Election Study, reviewing editor of PNAS Nexus, and sits on the advisory panel of the British Election Study. In 2024, he received an Andrew Carnegie fellowship to support a co-authored book project titled American Mosaic.

item.title: Brooke Moore
item.description:
Brooke Moore

Director of Sponsored Research Administration

Email: bmoore@iq.harvard.edu

Brooke joined the finance team at IQSS in 2014 and is currently the Director of Sponsored Research Administration. At IQSS, Brooke manages the sponsored research team and overall program. She is responsible for overseeing the financial management and research compliance of the sponsored research portfolio and providing pre-award support as needed. Brooke is also the administrative lead on several of IQSS’s scientific research programs.

item.title: Bruce Huang
item.description:
Bruce Huang

Data Science Lecturer, Harvard Extension School

Dr. Bruce Huang serves as director of the master’s degree program in information technology at Harvard Extension School, overseeing five ALM degree programs including computer science, cybersecurity, data science, digital media design, and systems engineering.

He is described as “a scholar-practitioner in the field of computer science.” As a practitioner, he developed software products at IBM and his tech startups focused on enabling enterprises to test and manage performance of mission-critical infrastructure. He served as “a managing partner and practice executive at IBM Global Services” and was a VC-backed tech and education entrepreneur. He “was named to the 2020 MIT Alumni Association Honor Roll of Service.”

item.title: Bruno S Sergi
item.description:
Bruno S Sergi

Instructor, DCE; Co-director, LEAD

Bruno S. Sergi is an instructor at Harvard University who teaches development economics and emerging markets courses. His research focuses on the political economy of emerging markets, covering investments, sustainable development, technology, institutional transparency, corruption, and global development practices. He chairs and co-directs the Lab for Entrepreneurship and Development (LEAD) in Cambridge, USA.

His advisory work spans public and private sectors, and he has served as economic coach of The South East Europe Trade Union Economic Experts Network since 2009. He edits Cambridge Elements in the Economics of Emerging Markets (Cambridge University Press) and serves as Associate Editor of The American Economist. He has authored, co-authored, or edited over thirty books and 200 scholarly papers.

item.title: Building terraFlow: How an Idea in the Lab Grew Into a Venture-Backed Startup
item.description: Dan Freeman, a Harvard PhD student in Biology and Biomedical Sciences, had prior experience with single-cell technology and pharma trials. Convinced there was a better approach, he began experimenting with artificial intelligence and arrived at his breakthrough concept. His vision involved using AI to accelerate drug discovery, and he had developed an early prototype. What he needed was guidance on commercialization—identifying customers, refining his pitch, and building a business plan. The IQSS Startup Foundry provided that support.

item.title: Call for Papers: 2026 CGA Conference
item.description: The Center for Geographic Analysis has issued a call for paper submissions for its 2026 conference, marking a special milestone as the center celebrates its 20th anniversary. The conference theme—past, present, and future—invites researchers to reflect on two decades of innovation in geographic analysis while exploring emerging frontiers in geospatial science and technology. Submissions are welcome from across all disciplines that use geographic analysis, spatial data, and mapping technologies in their research.

item.title: Call for Proposals: Dataverse Community Meeting 2025
item.description:
The Dataverse Project is excited to announce a call for proposals for the 2025 Dataverse Community Meeting, which will be hosted at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. This annual gathering is the premier event for the global Dataverse community, and the program committee invites submissions from repository administrators, developers, researchers, data professionals, and anyone working with or interested in the Dataverse platform.

Proposals are welcome across a wide range of topics related to research data management, open science infrastructure, and the Dataverse ecosystem. Potential topics include case studies of Dataverse implementations, technical presentations on new features or integrations, discussions of data curation workflows, explorations of policy and governance challenges, and demonstrations of tools or extensions. Both individual presentations and panel sessions are encouraged, with formats ranging from traditional talks to interactive workshops and hands-on tutorials.

item.title: Candace Fleming
item.description:
Candace Fleming

IQSS Startup Foundry Executive Fellow

Candace Fleming is an Executive Fellow in the Harvard IQSS Startup Foundry, working “at the intersection of data, innovation, and entrepreneurship.” She has over twenty years of experience as a finance and operations leader, helping build and scale companies by transforming complex ideas into practical, high-impact businesses.

She has served as CEO and COO across multiple ventures, including co-founding Crimson Hexagon with Gary King, leading fundraising, operational strategy, and team development efforts. Her work centers on data-driven decision-making and execution, especially in early-stage environments.

item.title: Caterina Stamoulis
item.description:
Caterina Stamoulis

Associate Professor of Pediatrics, HMS

Dr. Stamoulis’ research interests are at the intersection of Computational Cognitive Neuroscience and Data Science. She leads multiple projects that together aim to elucidate the evolving neural circuitry of the typically/atypically developing brain that supports cognitive function across domains, using large-scale brain datasets and novel computational tools. A recent research direction in her laboratory aims to bridge Neuroscience with the Social Sciences through Data Science and elucidate the impact of the individual brain’s topological organization (the connectome) on group/collective behaviors (e.g., cooperation).

item.title: Ce Gao
item.description:
Ce Gao

Dept of Chinese Literature, Peking University

Intellectual history of pre-modern China and database of digital humanity (CBDB)

item.title: Ceilyn Boyd
item.description:
Ceilyn Boyd

Interim Director of Data Science and Product Research

Email: cboyd@iq.harvard.edu

Ceilyn Boyd is the Dataverse Development Project Manager at Harvard University’s Institute for Quantitative Social Sciences (IQSS), overseeing the software development process to ensure the team meets its project, partnership, and grant responsibilities.

Previously, Boyd established and led the Harvard Library Research Data Services Program, which connects the Harvard community to resources and services throughout the research data lifecycle. Additional work at Harvard Library included taxonomy development, management of large-scale manuscript digitization projects, oversight of library collections as data initiatives, and leadership of major cross-organization strategic portfolios.

item.title: CGA creates Congressional District COVID-19 Dashboard
item.description: The Center for Geographic Analysis has created a comprehensive public dashboard that tracks COVID-19 data by congressional district, providing policymakers, researchers, and the public with geographically granular information about the pandemic’s spread and impact across the United States. This innovative tool fills a critical gap in COVID-19 data visualization by organizing information at the congressional district level, enabling more effective policy responses and helping lawmakers understand how the pandemic affects their constituents.

item.title: CGA develops RINX: Open-Source Solution for Big Raster Datasets
item.description: The Center for Geographic Analysis has developed RINX (Raster Index), an innovative open-source solution designed to address critical challenges in processing and analyzing big raster datasets from Earth observation systems. As satellite imagery and remote sensing data grow exponentially in volume and resolution, researchers face increasing technical barriers to working with these valuable resources. RINX provides an efficient indexing and retrieval system that makes large-scale raster analysis more accessible to the geospatial science community.

item.title: CGA Geographic Insights Lab Launches Initiative with Indian Government
item.description: The CGA Geographic Insights Lab has launched a significant initiative with the Government of India, with India Policy Insights being designated as a Key Initiative of NITI Aayog, the premier policy think tank of the Indian government. This partnership represents a major collaboration between Harvard researchers and Indian policymakers to leverage geospatial data and analysis for evidence-based governance and development planning across one of the world’s most populous and diverse nations.

item.title: CGA Project Selected for NSF Challenge
item.description: A Center for Geographic Analysis project focused on mapping geographical locations for successful market entry has been selected as a winner of the NSF I-GUIDE Spatial AI Challenge. This recognition highlights the innovative application of spatial artificial intelligence and geographic analysis techniques to solve real-world business and economic development challenges. The project demonstrates how advanced geospatial methods can provide actionable insights for organizations seeking to optimize their location decisions.

item.title: CGA releases Twitter Sentiment Geographical Index
item.description:
The Center for Geographic Analysis has released the Twitter Sentiment Geographical Index, an innovative tool that derives well-being indicators from social media data to track emotional patterns and public sentiment across geographic regions. This project demonstrates how large-scale analysis of publicly available social media posts can complement traditional surveys and administrative data to provide more timely, granular insights into population well-being and how it varies across space.

The Twitter Sentiment Geographical Index employs natural language processing and sentiment analysis techniques to categorize the emotional content of tweets, then aggregates these sentiment scores at various geographic scales from neighborhoods to cities to regions. By analyzing millions of social media posts over time, researchers can identify patterns in population mood, track responses to events or policies, and detect geographic variations in subjective well-being that might not be captured by conventional data sources. The tool provides a near-real-time window into collective emotional states across communities.

item.title: CGA Welcomes New Executive Director Dr. Rachel Franklin
item.description: Starting March 3, 2025, geographer Dr. Rachel Franklin will join the Center for Geographic Analysis (CGA), part of the Institute for Quantitative Social Science (IQSS) at Harvard University, as Executive Director. Franklin succeeds Dr. Wendy Guan and will lead all operations of Harvard’s largest organization focused on geographic research, technology, and teaching, collaborating with Professor S.V. Subramanian, chair of the CGA Faculty Advisory Group. The CGA provides consultation services, technical training, platform development, and sponsored research to support geospatial analysis and GIS projects across the University.

item.title: CGA: Geospatial Infrastructure Enhancement
item.description:
The Center for Geographic Analysis has undertaken a major geospatial infrastructure enhancement project to address growing demand for robust, scalable systems capable of handling geospatial big data. As researchers across disciplines increasingly work with massive spatial datasets—from high-resolution satellite imagery to detailed geographic information about billions of people and places—the technical infrastructure supporting this work must evolve to keep pace with data volume, velocity, and complexity.

The infrastructure enhancement encompasses multiple dimensions including expanded storage capacity, high-performance computing resources optimized for spatial operations, improved data management systems, and enhanced tools for large-scale geoprocessing. These improvements enable researchers to tackle questions that would be computationally infeasible with traditional GIS infrastructure, such as analyzing decades of daily satellite imagery for the entire planet or modeling complex spatial-temporal phenomena at fine geographic scales. The enhanced infrastructure supports both individual research projects and shared services that benefit the broader Harvard research community.

item.title: Charlotte Duffee
item.description:
Charlotte Duffee

Research Associate, Human Flourishing Program

Charlotte Duffee is a historian and philosopher of medicine whose research centers on how Western conceptions of suffering have evolved and shaped American medical practice. She earned her Ph.D. in the history and philosophy of science from the University of Toronto and also holds degrees from the New School and New York University. Her scholarship has been published in journals including the American Journal of Bioethics, PAIN, Bioethics, and the History of Medicine and Allied Sciences.

item.title: Chase H. Harrison
item.description:
Chase H. Harrison

Associate Director, Program on Survey Research

IQSS Faculty Affiliate. For full profile details, see the IQSS People directory.

item.title: Chengxi Yan
item.description:
Chengxi Yan

Fellow, CBDB; PhD candidate, Peking University

Chengxi Yan is a fellow in the China Biographical Database whose research focuses on “natural language processing, information visualization and digital humanities.” His current research interest involves constructing automatic workflows for analysis and mining of ancient texts using deep learning and complex network theory.

item.title: Chetan Krishna
item.description:
Chetan Krishna

Research Associate, Laboratory for Innovation Science

Chetan Krishna is a research associate focusing on the processes of science and technology commercialization and the adoption of AI/ML/NLP in businesses. His interests lie broadly in innovation and energy/sustainability. Chetan received his master’s degree from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s Technology Policy Program and received a bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi.

item.title: Chika Okafor
item.description:
Chika Okafor

Postdoctoral Fellow, NBER

As an economist and a lawyer with diverse policy expertise, Chika Okafor uses the tools of economics, law, and public policy to explore foundational matters of justice—with recent research spanning economic inequality, criminal justice, and climate change. Methodologically, his scholarship integrates economic theory, empirical techniques, and legal analysis to uncover mechanisms of—as well as inform solutions to—major economic and social problems impacting contemporary American society.

item.title: Chris Felton
item.description:
Chris Felton

Postdoctoral Fellow in Education, GSE

Chris’s work develops and showcases methods for drawing causal conclusions from observational data when identification assumptions are suspect. He is particularly interested in applying these methods to sociological questions related to suicide and mental health in the US. In the past, he has worked on instrumental variables methods and the interrupted time series design. He is currently working on panel data methods for causal inference with Luke Miratrix.

item.title: Christina Hinton
item.description:
Christina Hinton

Research Affiliate, Human Flourishing Program

Dr. Christina Hinton leads the Human Flourishing Program’s work in education and parenting. At Harvard, she leads research on character skills, loving relationships, and flourishing among children, adolescents, educators and parents internationally. In addition, she leads the Evidence-Based Parenting for Flourishing Families initiative. Dr. Hinton is also the Founder and CEO of Research Schools International (RSI), which has carried out over 50 research and professional development projects to promote character skills and flourishing in schools across 70 countries. She lectures internationally and has delivered keynotes in over 35 countries. Prior to her current roles, Dr. Hinton was a faculty member at Harvard Graduate School of Education, lecturing on neuroscience and education and social-emotional learning. In addition, she worked in multilateral diplomacy and international policymaking at the OECD’s Center for Educational Research and Innovation and UNICEF’s Early Childhood Development unit. She was also a Research Fellow at Sesame Workshop. Dr. Hinton completed her doctorate and master’s at Harvard in education, neuroscience, and child development, and her bachelors at Swarthmore in neuroscience and education.

item.title: Christina J Cross
item.description:
Christina J Cross

Assistant Professor of Sociology, FAS

IQSS Faculty Affiliate. For full profile details, see the IQSS People directory.

item.title: Christine Choirat
item.description:
Christine Choirat

Senior Research Scientist, Harvard Chan SPH

I am a Senior Research Scientist at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and at the Institute for Quantitative Social Science.

I was trained as a statistician (PhD 2003, Paris Dauphine). My research interests are data science and high-performance computing, reproducible research, and environmental policy and health policy.

Recent published works include the New England Journal of Medicine, the Journal of the American Medical Association, and the Annals of Applied Statistics.

item.title: Christoph Lange
item.description:
Christoph Lange

Professor of Biostatistics

Dr. Lange’s research interests span statistical genetics and generalized linear models. Recent work in statistical genetics includes family-based association tests, meta-analysis of linkage studies, GEE-methods in linkage analysis, and marker-assisted selection. In family-based association tests (FBATs), he has focused on developing power calculations for family-based association studies, multivariate extensions of the FBAT statistic, FBATs for time-to-onset data, and approaches to the multiple testing problem in family-based studies. He is also involved in collaborative research in asthma genetics and COPD genetics.

item.title: Christoph Mikulaschek
item.description:
Christoph Mikulaschek

Assistant Professor, Department of Government

Christoph Mikulaschek’s research interests focus on international security and the political economy of international organizations. He received the APSA Merze Tate Award for the best dissertation in international relations. His work has appeared in the American Journal of Political Science, International Organization, the Journal of Conflict Resolution, and the Review of International Organization. He holds a PhD in political science from Princeton University.

item.title: Christopher Avery
item.description:
Christopher Avery

Roy E. Larsen Professor of Public Policy, HKS

Email: chris_avery@harvard.edu

Chris N. Avery, Roy E. Larsen Professor of Public Policy, teaches analytic courses in microeconomics and statistics. He studies “rating and selection mechanisms, focusing on the college admissions system.” His first book, The Early Admissions Game, coauthored with Andrew Fairbanks and Richard Zeckhauser, was published by Harvard University Press in March 2003. In his current research, he studies “college application patterns and college enrollment choices for high school students.” He completed a PhD in economic analysis at the Stanford Business School and holds prior degrees from Harvard and Cambridge universities.

item.title: Christopher Winship
item.description:
Christopher Winship

Diker-Tishman Professor of Sociology

Diker-Tishman Professor of Sociology, was born in Topeka, Kansas and grew up in New Britain, Connecticut. He did his undergraduate work in sociology and mathematics at Dartmouth College and his graduate work in this department, receiving his degree in 1977. After leaving Harvard he did a one year post-doctoral fellowship at the Institute for Research on Poverty at the University of Wisconsin and a two-year fellowship at the National Opinion Research Center (NoRC) at the University of Chicago. In 1980 he joined the Sociology Department at Northwestern University. During his twelve years at Northwestern he was Director of the Program in Mathematical Methods in the Social Sciences and for four years chair of the Department of Sociology. He was a founding member of Northwestern’s Department of Statistics, and held a courtesy appointment in Economics. From 1984 to 1986 he was Director of the Economics Research Center at NoRC. He has been a member of the Harvard department since 1992, and, since 2002, at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government (HKS). He is currently doing research on several topics: The Ten Point Coalition, a group of black ministers who are working with the Boston police to reduce youth violence; statistical models for causal analysis; the effects of education on mental ability; causes of the racial difference in performance in elite colleges and universities; changes in the racial differential in imprisonment rates over the past sixty years.

item.title: Chunling Lu
item.description:
Chunling Lu

Associate Professor of Medicine, HMS

Chunling Lu, Ph.D., is a health economist at Harvard Medical School holding assistant professor positions in medicine and global health and social medicine. Her research spans five areas: tracking and analyzing “national and global funding sources for health;” developing methodologies and cost-collecting technologies for evaluation research; “evaluating the impact of global health aid on health system strengthening” in resource-poor settings; evaluating universal health coverage progress; and “measuring the economic burden of diseases in developing countries.”

item.title: Class of 2026 at IQSS: Whats Next?
item.description:
The IQSS community includes affiliated graduate students across Harvard University engaged in social science research. As the academic year ends, some graduate students complete their programs and move on. Below are updates from graduating affiliates continuing their work beyond Harvard.

Dorothy Manevich (PhD, Government, American Politics)

Dorothy is joining the national political department of the United Autoworkers Union (UAW).

Jeremiah Cha (PhD, Government)

In the fall, Jeremiah will join the Center for the Study of Democratic Politics at Princeton University.

item.title: Claudine Gay
item.description:
Claudine Gay

Wilbur A Cowett Professor of Government

Gay is described as “a leading scholar of political behavior, considering issues of race and politics in America” who has been a professor of Government and of African and African-American Studies at Harvard since 2006. Her research explores how the election of minority officeholders affects citizens’ perceptions of government, how neighborhood environments shape racial and political attitudes among Black Americans, the roots of competition and cooperation between minority groups (particularly between Black Americans and Latinos), and the consequences of housing mobility programs for political participation among the poor. She brings these interests to her teaching, including courses on Post-Civil Rights Black Politics, Democratic Citizenship, and Politics of Race, Ethnicity and Immigration. She is “founding chair of the Inequality in America Initiative, a multidisciplinary effort launched in 2017.”

item.title: Clemens Havas
item.description:
Clemens Havas

Visiting Fellow, CGA

Clemens Havas is a PhD candidate at University of Salzburg’s Department of Geoinformatics – Z_GIS with a background in computer science. He specializes in combining state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms with geospatial analysis to extract information about large-scale events like a natural disaster. The information is provided in near real-time after the outbreak of an event by utilizing new data sources like social media networks.

item.description:
Colleen Mathis

Affiliate

IQSS Visitor/Affiliate.

item.title: Community Announcement: New Space Arrangements at IQSS
item.description:
IQSS is pleased to announce new space arrangements in the CGIS Knafel Building designed to better serve the research community as we adapt to post-pandemic work patterns and embrace more flexible approaches to office space utilization. These changes reflect lessons learned during the pandemic about how researchers work most effectively and acknowledge the evolving needs of our community as members balance in-person collaboration with remote work flexibility.

The new arrangements include a hybrid approach to office space that accommodates both dedicated workspace for staff and programs while providing bookable desk space for affiliated researchers who need on-campus work areas on a flexible basis. This system enables more efficient use of IQSS facilities while ensuring that community members have access to professional workspace when they need it. The changes also support collaboration by creating more shared spaces where researchers can connect with colleagues, access specialized resources, and participate in the intellectual life of the institute.

item.title: Computer Lab FAQs
item.description:
Can I eat in the lab?

Food is not permitted in the labs. Please stay hydrated but dispose of any food outside of the lab to keep the area free of pests that also love to consume wires.

Can I print to lab printers from my personal computer?

Yes. You must select hmdc-crimson-print to be able to print to our printers. Instructions are available for both Windows and macOS laptops.

item.title: Connie Chen
item.description:
Connie Chen

Preceptor in Geospatial Analysis, Department of Government

Connie Chen is a preceptor in spatial analysis in the Government Department at Harvard University and an associate with Harvard’s Center for Geographic Analysis (CGA). She earned a PhD in Urban and Regional Planning from the University of Florida, an MS in Geography (Urban and Regional Planning) from Peking University, and a Bachelor’s degree in Landscape Gardening from Beijing Forestry University.

item.title: Connor Jerzak
item.description:
Connor Jerzak

Visiting Assistant Professor, Department of Government

IQSS Faculty Affiliate. For full profile details, see the IQSS People directory.
